content: The passage explains that sorting a small number of elements (e.g., six) is quick, but sorting very large numbers (like six billion) takes much longer. To analyze this, we parameterize sorting time based on input size, examining how running time behaves as the input grows. Importantly, we focus on finding upper bounds for running time—knowing the maximum time a program will take—because this provides users with a reliable guarantee on performance, which is especially crucial in real-time applications. Without an upper bound, users lack confidence about how long the program might run.
